## About us

We started in 2016 in a rented office above a dental practice in Providence, because that's where our first customer was.

Three of us had spent years building software for hospitals. The clinics we visited had a different problem. A hospital can afford a full-time scheduler; a six-provider family practice cannot. So the front desk does it — between check-ins, insurance calls, and the fax machine nobody can decommission. Double-bookings happen. No-shows go unnoticed until a room sits empty for forty minutes.

[COMPANY] handles the calendar so the front desk can handle people.

We do a few things and try to do them properly. Patients book and reschedule themselves from their phones, at whatever hour suits them. Reminders go out by text and email; confirmations come back into the same chart. Templates fit how your clinic actually runs — sixty-minute new-patient slots, double-booked follow-ups on Thursdays, Dr. Okonkwo out every other Friday. When someone cancels, the waitlist fills the slot without anyone phoning down a list.

We're HIPAA-compliant, we sign BAAs, and we'll tell you exactly where your data lives.

Today about 900 clinics use us, most of them under ten providers: family medicine, physical therapy, dermatology, behavioral health. We're 34 people, remote across nine states, and roughly a third came out of clinic operations rather than tech. That shows up in the product, and in support — you get a person who knows what a superbill is.

No sales call required to see pricing. It's on the site.
